title: Split pieces compute each fibre stalk
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ satisfy $t\mathbin{\gg}f=y$. For the cofiltered category of split neighbourhoods defined in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-split-neighbourhoods-cofinal], the functor taking a neighbourhood to its $t$-th piece, pointed by $(u,t)$, is initial into the category of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $t$.

source.place: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.SplitNbhd.initial_pieceFunctor; the existing fully proved split-neighbourhood argument underlying Stacks Tag 03QP (1)

proof.text: For any pointed etale neighbourhood of t, choose an affine chart of a split base neighbourhood. Its t-th piece is the spectrum of the finite algebra quotient by the complementary idempotent and has a unique geometric fibre point.

Shrink the given neighbourhood over that piece to an affine etale algebra. The existing algebraic etale section theorem produces a further etale base refinement and a map from its t-th piece into the chosen neighbourhood, preserving the marked point. This is exists_pieceFunctor_obj_hom.
Common split refinements and the piece equalizer theorem equalize competing maps. The cofiltered initial-functor criterion yields initial_pieceFunctor.
